reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the original § 7(a) caps Contractor at fees actually paid under a single Statement of Work with no 12-month look-back, no USD 1,000,000 floor, no 'paid or payable' basis, and its only carve-out is a cross-reference (Paragraph 9) that does not deliver confidentiality/IP/gross negligence/fraud carve-outs — below the walk-away threshold on Vendor cap and carve-outs.

Redline reaches the preferred position: mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, an uncapped 'Excluded Claims' definition covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, plus confirmation that Company's fee payments are not damages subject to the cap.

The 0.940 changed-character ratio is acceptable here: the whole of § 7(a) is the cap language, and changing the basis, making it mutual and inserting the carve-out sentence necessarily replaces those two sentences; scope is confined to the cap sentence and § 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion is left intact.

Drafting is directionally correct for the Customer (broadens 'arising out of or relating to this Agreement', removes the SOW-only limitation, keeps ALL-CAPS formatting and uses (I)/(II) to avoid conflicting with the subsection lettering); the modest increase in Company's own cap to the USD 1,000,000 floor is the playbook's own preferred mutual formulation.

Comment is accurate, concise and on-tone: it explains the mutual cap, the reason the SOW-limited cap is inadequate, the substitution of real carve-outs for the broken Paragraph 9 cross-reference, and the payment-obligations clarification, and the fallback is preserved in the rationale for negotiation.
